value.content: {"id": "portswigger_http_smuggling", "item_type": "methodology", "topic": "http_request_smuggling", "category": "PortSwigger Web Security: HTTP Request Smuggling", "name": "HTTP Request Smuggling (CL.TE, TE.CL, TE.TE & HTTP/2) Methodology", "cwe": "CWE-444", "owasp_category": "A04:2021 - Insecure Design", "signals": ["front_end_reverse_proxy", "dual_content_length_transfer_encoding", "obfuscated_transfer_encoding", "http2_downgrade_to_http11", "backend_request_timeout"], "verification_strategy": "Transmit differential non-destructive HTTP requests with both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding: chunked headers. Observe backend timeout delays (e.g. 5-10s) indicating parsing divergence between frontend proxy and backend server.", "evidence_requirements": ["differential_timeout_delay", "pipelined_prefix_response_mutation", "http_version_downgrade_log"], "tools": [{"tool": "smuggler", "cmd": "python3 smuggler.py -u https://example.com -m POST", "desc": "Audits CL.TE, TE.CL, and header obfuscation smuggling variations"}, {"tool": "httpx", "cmd": "httpx -u url -http2 -probe", "desc": "Verifies HTTP/2 protocol support and proxy downgrade characteristics"}], "remediation": "Prioritize end-to-end HTTP/2 without protocol downgrade. If HTTP/1.1 is required, configure frontend and backend servers to reject requests containing both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers.", "description": "PortSwigger HTTP Request Smuggling curriculum explores CL.TE and TE.CL desynchronization vulnerabilities, obfuscating Transfer-Encoding headers (TE.TE), weaponizing smuggling for cache poisoning, credential theft, and HTTP/2 request tunneling."}
